Here, Plaintiffs are 17 proceeding under the second theory—i.e., failure to conform with promises and affirmations. 18 Plaintiffs describe O.P.M.S. kratom as failing to conform with the “implied affirmations of 19 fact . . . that the Products are not addictive and do not cause withdrawals.” Compl., ¶ 141. But the 20 entire theory behind the Complaint is that Martian Sales did not tell end-users in its packaging that 21 Kratom was potentially addictive and/or could cause withdrawal symptoms. Plaintiffs cannot 22 premise their implied warranty claim on the notion that kratom failed to conform with promises or 23 affirmations that were never actually made. 24 25 26 4 Further, there is a split of authority in California district courts as to whether the CLRA claim could also be dismissed for lacking privity between the end-consumer (Plaintiffs) and the 27 manufacturer (Martian Sales).
